note: Files: A = s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl and B = s3 r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl, read from runs/theory-rows/s3new/... if present, otherwise fetched to runs/theory-tests/s3new/... (same S3 object). Subjects come from studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Main ambiguity: per_problem.json's subject values are lowercase with underscores ('number_theory', 62 problems). No value equals 'Number Theory', so the literal filter subject != 'Number Theory' drops nothing, and the main number keeps Number Theory problems. alt_measured drops subject 'number_theory', which is almost certainly what was meant. Expect the two numbers to differ, because Number Theory texts are full of modular arithmetic of the 'a*b = c' form, which the post-filters only partly remove. Every row in both files has sample 0, so the smallest-sample rule for B has no effect. cap_hit is a bool in every row and 'false' was tested as cap_hit is False. The EQ regexes were copied verbatim from the decoded recipe; the pre-check character set includes a real newline. The bootstrap resamples the S problems, each entry being a paired (A, B) count tuple. A resample with N = 0 returns inf or 0 rather than failing. n = |S|, and both groups have the same size.

Files: A = s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base, cue, T 1.0) and C = s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL, plain, T 1.0), fetched as in p1, plus per_problem.json. Same main ambiguity as p1: no subject equals 'Number Theory' (the file uses 'number_theory'), so the main number excludes nothing and alt_measured excludes 'number_theory'. The statistic is RL rate over base rate, and refuted_by_met = statistic > 0.8. The EQ procedure is the same code as in p1. One caveat: T2 texts also begin with ' line!', even though the inventory calls T2 'plain'. The recipe is applied as written anyway. The bootstrap is over the paired S problems, and n = |S|.

Files: E = studies/rlneurons/results/egate/math500_lo6-01/rows.jsonl and D = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (both committed). Main ambiguity: E numbers its samples 1-4 and D numbers them 0-3. The seeds match this numbering (E 610s0pid, D 410s0pid, s = sample). The literal 'same sample' pairing therefore matches E samples 1-3 to D samples 1-3 and drops E sample 4 for lack of a partner, so at most 3 pairs per problem. alt_measured pairs E sample s with D sample s-1 (all 4). E rows have no attempt field, so only D is filtered on attempt == 0. cap_hit is present in every row, so the finish_reason fallback is never used. wrong = 1 unless score_v3 == 1, using the stored score_v3; nothing is regraded. The statistic is a mean over kept pairs. The bootstrap resamples problems, each entry being the list of that problem's kept pairs, and only problems with at least one kept pair are included. n = number of kept pairs (each group has that many rows).

Files: H = studies/rlneurons/results/egate/math500_hi6-01/rows.jsonl (samples 1-2) and D = day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (samples 0-3, attempt 0). Literal same-sample pairing matches H samples 1 and 2 to D samples 1 and 2. alt_measured pairs H sample s with D sample s-1 (D samples 0 and 1). Cap hit, wrong, bootstrap and n are as in p3. refuted_by_met = statistic > 0.017.
